title: Understanding Lagrange Multipliers
teaching_need: First-year students can perform the algebra of constrained optimisation without understanding why the multiplier method works, what its geometric relationships mean or when its conclusions are justified.
intended_capability: Interpret constrained optimisation problems; connect feasible sets, gradients, tangency and multiplier equations; solve manageable problems accurately; distinguish stationary candidates from proven optima; recognise limitations; and transfer the method independently.
summary: A 90-minute Learning Journey for first-year quantitative learners that moves from constrained-choice reasoning through geometry and formal equations to diagnosing unsupported claims and independently establishing a justified global optimum—without a Learning Journal.
primary_pattern: Concrete → Visual → Formal → Transfer, with explicit evaluation of mathematical claims before independent transfer
supporting_patterns: Concrete constrained-choice reasoning before formal multiplier algebra
Visual treatment of gradients, tangency and feasible sets
Connection from geometry to formal Lagrange equations
Explicit evaluation of what a calculation does and does not prove
Diagnosis of mathematical claims and unsupported conclusions
Independent transfer requiring justification of a global optimum, not only a stationary candidate
learning_sequence: Overview — orientation to constrained optimisation and journey expectations
Why the constraint matters (Interactive) — constrained-choice reasoning with a familiar problem
Seeing gradients and tangency (Interactive) — visual relationships among feasible sets, gradients and optima
From geometry to the multiplier equations (Expository) — connect geometric insight to formal equations
What does the calculation prove? (Expository) — distinguish candidate solutions from justified optima
Diagnosing mathematical claims (Assessment Pack) — evaluate claims about constrained optimisation
Independent constrained optimisation (Assessment Pack) — apply the method and justify a global optimum
transferable_principle: When learners can execute a formal procedure without knowing what it justifies, develop judgement by moving Concrete → Visual → Formal → Transfer and inserting an explicit evaluation of claims before independent application—so the culminating task requires establishing and justifying a global optimum, not merely calculating a stationary candidate. The Lagrange topic is the vehicle; the judgement-before-transfer logic travels.
